passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Sea otters use rocks to crack open shellfish.
• Some crows bend twigs into hooks to pull insects from tree bark.
• Chimpanzees use sticks to fish termites out of their mounds.
• All three animals use these objects to get food.
stem: The student wants to make a generalization about tool use in animals. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choices: Several kinds of animals, including sea otters, crows, and chimpanzees, use objects as tools to get food.
Chimpanzees use sticks to fish termites out of their mounds, which is a clever way to get food.
Some crows bend twigs into hooks so that they can pull insects out from under tree bark.
Sea otters use rocks to crack open shellfish, and chimpanzees use sticks to catch termites.
steps: A generalization is a broad statement that covers several cases.
The correct choice states the pattern across all three animals.
The others describe one or two specific examples without making a general statement.
key: A generalization moves from examples to a broad claim.
